correctness.rationale: From the actual Git RESULT.md blob b26f24e194e2cfa019ce15b39e938b50223adc07, reconstruct W(z)=log((1−z²)/(1+z²)), which is analytic because the quotient maps the disk into the right half-plane. W′(z)=−4z/(1−z⁴); CR gives u_y=−8/π Re[z/(1−z⁴)], whence the claimed Jacobian. For |z|≤r, Re[z/(1−z⁴)]≤|z|/(1−|z|^4)≤r/(1−r⁴), and equality for r>0 forces |z|=r,z^4=r^4 and positive-real quotient, hence unique z=r. Strict radial increase yields J>0 inside r_M and J=0 at positive real r_M. F_M(x+iy)=x+iY_x(y) fixes x and each vertical disk slice is connected; ∂_yY_x=J>0 gives global injectivity. For r>r_M the larger disk contains a Jacobian zero, contradicting Lewy’s necessary nonzero-Jacobian theorem for injective harmonic maps. No finite grid is needed. Independently differentiated the rational kernel and checked the equality/radial monotonicity argument; separate Resultary fiber-valence analysis confirms the same explicit shear, without substituting for this full-disk proof.
residual_risks: The claim is for centered Euclidean disks D_r within the unit disk; it does not classify all non-centered injective domains or universal Landau radii.
